correctness.rationale: The five equispaced illumination-cone bisectors and strict 3π/5 opening give exactly adjacent pairs of illuminated vertices per planar direction. Cartesian product tangent-cone interiors factor; every 4D direction is contained in a cyclic 2×2 tile. Every one of five rows requires three tile incidences, and each tile hits two rows, so at least eight directions. The eight explicit tiles cover all 25 vertices (independently checked by exact integer script). Fractional weight ≥25/4 follows from four-vertex maximum; all 25 tiles of weight 1/4 attain it. The active-facet argument extends vertex coverage to all boundary points. Quantifiers and degenerate directions are covered; no finite sampling is used for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The theorem solves two standard invariants across the complete natural family of products of two equiangular pentagons, including nonregular deformations. Its strict 8<3·3 counterexample identifies a concrete product-law phenomenon beyond separate factor numbers. The exact 25/4 fractional value and row-incidence obstruction explain a nontrivial integrality gap and yield a transferable cyclic torus covering model. This is a motivated geometric class and complete exact invariant, not an arbitrary tiny numerical gain.
